headline: YouTuber Touhid Afridi arrested in fraud case
summary: Popular content creator Touhid Afridi has been taken into custody by police following allegations of fraud.
details: Popular YouTuber Touhid Afridi has been arrested by law enforcement agencies in connection with a fraud case.
The arrest comes after legal complaints were filed against him regarding fraudulent activities.
Police have taken him into custody for further investigation into the claims made in the case.
Details regarding the specific nature of the fraud and the victims involved are currently being processed by the authorities.

headline_marked: Writ filed to [[challenge Ad-din Hospital's licence cancellation]]
headline: Writ filed to challenge Ad-din Hospital's licence cancellation
summary: A public interest petition has been filed at the High Court seeking a review of the government's decision to shut down the Moghbazar-based facility.
details: A lawyer has filed a petition at the High Court challenging the government's decision to cancel the licence of Ad-din Medical College Hospital in Dhaka's Moghbazar.
The petition, filed in the public interest by Senior Advocate Yunus Ali Akhand, seeks a review of the shutdown order.
The government scrapped the hospital's licence on June 11 following the deaths of six newborns at the facility.
The newborns died within a few hours at a post-operative ward early on May 27, leading to allegations of negligence.
A case was filed at Ramna Police Station by the father of one of the deceased newborns.
The Ministry of Health and the hospital administration have both formed committees to investigate the incident.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) had previously stated that the hospital had 30 days to challenge the cancellation.
caption:
Six newborns died within hours at a Dhaka hospital, leading to its licence being scrapped. Now, a legal battle begins to reopen it.

A lawyer has filed a petition at the High Court challenging the government's decision to cancel the licence of Ad-din Medical College Hospital in Dhaka's Moghbazar.

The petition, filed in the public interest by Senior Advocate Yunus Ali Akhand, seeks a review of the shutdown order.

The government scrapped the hospital's licence on June 11 following the deaths of six newborns at the facility.

The newborns died within a few hours at a post-operative ward early on May 27, leading to allegations of negligence.

A case was filed at Ramna Police Station by the father of one of the deceased newborns.

The Ministry of Health and the hospital administration have both formed committees to investigate the incident.

The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) had previously stated that the hospital had 30 days to challenge the cancellation.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #HealthCare #HighCourt #AdDinHospital #MedicalNegligence

Source: Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, Somoy News, The Daily Star
